was easier for me to move my medical records to Mercheford House and get an appointment there, than is was to even speak to someone competent at this disgrace of a health centre. It took less than 24 Hours to change practices and get to see someone face to face.

I have been a loyal patient at this surgery for over 40 years. For four decades, I have praised the doctors and the care provided here, but the recent "modernization" of their booking system has turned this practice into a fortress designed to keep patients out.
The surgery chose this system, yet they refuse to take any accountability for the chaos it has caused. The experience of trying to access healthcare here is now characterized by:

Administrative Gatekeeping: The new booking system is a total failure. Emails are ignored, and the phone lines are perpetually queued. When you finally do reach a human being, the receptionists are staggeringly blunt, condescending, and rude.
A Lack of Basic Compassion: When I raised legitimate concerns about the inability to book a simple appointment, I was told to "take it up with the government." This is a cowardly deflection. The government didn't choose this specific, broken software—the surgery management did.
The Death of Continuity: For a long-term patient, being told you can no longer book over the phone is a slap in the face. They have effectively barred the door to anyone who isn't willing to fight through a digital obstacle course.
It is a tragedy that such talented, fantastic doctors are being hidden behind an administrative wall of incompetence and hostility. You cannot provide "care" if you make it impossible for patients to reach you. After 40 years, I expected respect; instead, I received a "take it or leave it" attitude.
